name: Stormwind Library
summary: In Stormwind Keep, Donyal Tovald copies the kingdom’s histories for those bearing library scrips. Young King Anduin Wrynn funds the work, opening accounts of Azeroth to citizens and scholars.

sections.title: A Royal Mandate for Knowledge
sections.body: Young King Anduin directs royal funds toward learning. They pay for copies of ancient manuscripts and historical journals. In Stormwind Keep, the Royal Library preserves these accounts and copies them for those in royal service.

sections.title: The Scrip Exchange
sections.body: Hand copying delicate parchment takes time, ink, and royal sanction. Donyal Tovald accepts official library scrips issued to adventurers and scholars across Alliance territories. In return, he provides copies of historical works, from ancient Eastern Kingdoms histories to accounts of distant lands. These books tell of conflicts beyond the capital.

faq.q: What is the purpose of the Stormwind Library quest?
faq.answer: You can exchange a Library Scrip with librarian Donyal Tovald for a readable book. The books recount Alliance people, places, and events across Azeroth.
Donyal Tovald oversees the Royal Library in Stormwind Keep. He manages the kingdom’s written histories and distributes copies by King Anduin’s order.

faq.q: Where do you obtain a Library Scrip?
aliases: where do i get library scrip
faq.answer: Scholars, magistrates, and officials across Alliance territories give out Library Scrips to those who value learning about the wider world.

faq.q: Why is young King Anduin funding the library?
aliases: why does anduin care about books
faq.answer: King Anduin Wrynn funds copies of historical works because he values learning and education. Still a child, he set aside royal funds to make the kingdom’s histories available to the public, guided by Regent Bolvar Fordragon.

faq.q: Where is the library located in Stormwind?
faq.answer: The Royal Library lies inside Stormwind Keep, the great fortress in the eastern part of the city. Donyal Tovald can be found among its shelves and reading tables.

faq.q: Can I read the books I receive?
faq.answer: Yes. Each book from the library can be read, with background on legends and historical events across Azeroth.

angles.text: As a mage, you can turn to the Royal Library for the kingdom’s histories alongside your arcane studies in the Mage Quarter.
As an Alliance citizen, you can find records of the Alliance of Lordaeron’s triumphs and tragedies, and the bonds between humans, dwarves, gnomes, and high elves.

As a human, you know the value of preserving history. Old Stormwind lost countless archives when it was sacked during the First War. Now scholars protect and copy the histories that survived the kingdom’s rebuilding.
